headline: Sensex ends 252 points lower, Nifty below 22,650 as banking and pharma drag; IT stocks like Infosys rally

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Selling pressure in the banking, pharmaceutical, and automobile sectors dragged the major indices down
Bajaj Finance and HDFC Life shares each dropped by 3%, weighing heavily on the Sensex
Global investors remained cautious while awaiting the release of the latest US CPI inflation data
Foreign Institutional Investors are seeking specific triggers and better valuations before increasing Indian equity exposure
whatHappening: BHEL shares surged 4% following the announcement of the company's second-quarter financial results
GMR Aero Technic signed an MoU with a French firm to develop an Integrated Cabin Excellence Centre in Hyderabad
IT heavyweights Infosys and TCS rallied, providing a necessary cushion against a deeper market decline
The FDA suspended the license of a Domino's outlet in Parel, Mumbai, due to food safety violations
summary: The Indian stock market closed lower on October 14, with the Sensex falling 252 points and the Nifty ending below 22,650. Heavy selling in banking and pharma sectors was partially offset by gains in IT stocks like Infosys and TCS. Corporate highlights included BHEL's post-earnings rally and GMR's new strategic partnership in the aviation sector.
